title: The Economic Impact of the Cigarette Industry in Sri Lanka
gist: A consulting report commissioned by Ceylon Tobacco Company PLC estimates Sri Lanka's legal cigarette industry contributed Rs 74.0 billion to GDP, about 81,400 jobs (1% of employment) and Rs 181 billion in taxes (3.6% of national tax receipts) in 2025. Illicit cigarettes took an estimated 20% of the Factory Made Cigarette market, costing about Rs 29.5 billion in forgone tax revenue.

themes.theme: Fiscal weight of legal cigarettes in Sri Lanka

insights.claim: Sri Lanka's legal cigarette industry generated an estimated Rs 181 billion in tax revenues in 2025, equal to 3.6% of national tax receipts.
insights.speaker: Sanele Mjikane
insights.so_what: A single-producer industry supplying 3.6% of Sri Lankan tax receipts makes excise policy a material sovereign fiscal variable.
insights.quote: The industry also generated an estimated Rs 181 billion in tax revenues, accounting for 3.6% of national tax receipts.

insights.claim: Sri Lanka's legal cigarette industry's tax contribution (Rs 181 billion) is roughly 2.4 times its estimated GDP contribution (Rs 74.0 billion) in 2025, indicating the sector functions largely as a tax-collection channel.
insights.speaker: Sanele Mjikane
insights.so_what: Tax take far exceeding value added signals high excise dependence and sensitivity of state revenue to volume shifts.

insights.claim: Sri Lanka's legal cigarette industry contributed an estimated Rs 74.0 billion to GDP and supported around 81,400 jobs in 2025, equivalent to 1% of national employment.
insights.speaker: Sanele Mjikane
insights.so_what: Sizes the domestic economic stake in tobacco regulation decisions.
insights.quote: the legal cigarette industry contributed an estimated Rs 74.0 billion to Sri Lanka’s GDP and supported around 81,400 jobs, equivalent to 1% of national employment

insights.claim: The cigarette industry's economic footprint in Sri Lanka spans the full value chain from tobacco leaf cultivation and manufacturing to distribution and retail, with activity supported directly and via spending with domestic suppliers and employee wages.
insights.speaker: Sanele Mjikane
insights.so_what: Footprint figures include indirect and induced effects, so headline numbers are broader than the producer's own operations.

insights.claim: The consulting report on Sri Lanka's cigarette industry was commissioned by Ceylon Tobacco Company PLC, the industry's sole legal manufacturer, so its estimates are sponsor-funded analysis.
insights.speaker: Sanele Mjikane
insights.so_what: Sponsor-commissioned impact numbers are typically deployed in tax and regulatory lobbying and warrant independent cross-checks.

insights.speaker: Sanele Mjikane
insights.so_what: A one-fifth illicit share is a key argument against further excise hikes and a potential upside lever for enforcement-driven revenue.

insights.claim: Forgone tax from illicit cigarettes in Sri Lanka (about Rs 29.5 billion) equals roughly 16% of the legal industry's Rs 181 billion tax contribution in 2025.
insights.speaker: Sanele Mjikane
insights.so_what: Quantifies how much state revenue could be recaptured by curbing smuggling versus raising rates.
